react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is dominated by the tryptophan metabolic axis, with overwhelming cross-paradigm consensus. Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:map00380/hsa00380, WP:WP465) is the supreme winner: it achieves rank-1 in the RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR = 1.46×10⁻¹⁵, fold-enrichment 857.8, 6 metabolites hit), rank-1 in MetaboAnalystR KEGG ORA (p = 1.79×10⁻⁷, 5 metabolites hit), and rank-1 in the m/z-direct mummichog analysis (p = 0.0040, 8 compounds on the 15-member empirical network). The KEGG pathway identifier (hsa00380) is consistent across the two ORA tools, and mummichog maps its own MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism entry to the same KEGG compound set, confirming a true biological consensus rather than a namespace artefact. Five driver metabolites are verified in the pathway by the enrichment results: L-tryptophan (C00078), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), tryptamine (C00398), and indoleacetaldehyde (C00637). Quinolinic acid (C03722) additionally anchors the kynurenine branch feeding NAD+ biosynthesis (WP:WP4210, FDR 7.30×10⁻⁸). A tight sub-cluster of serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (Reactome R-HSA-209931, FDR 2.81×10⁻⁸) and biogenic amine synthesis (WP:WP550, FDR 3.60×10⁻⁸) emerges from the same input set, implicating the serotonergic and pineal neurochemical axes. The treatment condition is therefore most parsimoniously interpreted as a perturbation of tryptophan catabolism, with coordinated shifts in the serotonin–melatonin biosynthetic arm and the quinolinic acid kynurenine arm, consistent with neuroinflammatory or energy-metabolism stress contexts.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary over-representation analyses converge on Tryptophan metabolism as the dominant enriched pathway. KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) ranks first in RaMP ORA with an FDR of 1.46×10⁻¹⁵ and a fold-enrichment of 857.8, capturing six of the eleven input metabolites: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, and quinolinic acid. The same pathway reproduces as WP:WP465 (Tryptophan metabolism) in WikiPathways (FDR 4.93×10⁻¹², fold-enrichment 622.6) and as a sub-cluster within WP:WP3925 (Amino acid metabolism). The Reactome pathway R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis) appears as rank 5 in RaMP (FDR 2.81×10⁻⁸) and explicitly contains L-tryptophan, serotonin, and melatonin. Cross-paradigm consensus confirms that L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078) is the primary driver substrate feeding both the serotonergic arm (serotonin → melatonin) and the kynurenine arm (quinolinic acid → NAD+ biosynthesis via WP:WP4210). Succinic acid additionally anchors the TCA-cycle intersection (WP:WP3925 rank 2). The four-driver set (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, quinolinic acid) is consistent across KEGG, WikiPathways, and Reactome databases, establishing a robust multi-database signal for tryptophan catabolism perturbation.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is dominated by the tryptophan metabolic axis, with overwhelming cross-paradigm consensus. Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:map00380/hsa00380, WP:WP465) is the supreme winner: it achieves rank-1 in the RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR = 1.46×10⁻¹⁵, fold-enrichment 857.8, 6 metabolites hit), rank-1 in MetaboAnalystR KEGG ORA (p = 1.79×10⁻⁷, 5 metabolites hit), and rank-1 in the m/z-direct mummichog analysis (p = 0.0040, 8 compounds on the 15-member empirical network). The KEGG pathway identifier (hsa00380) is consistent across the two ORA tools, and mummichog maps its own MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism entry to the same KEGG compound set, confirming a true biological consensus rather than a namespace artefact. Five driver metabolites are verified in the pathway by the enrichment results: L-tryptophan (C00078), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), tryptamine (C00398), and indoleacetaldehyde (C00637). Quinolinic acid (C03722) additionally anchors the kynurenine branch feeding NAD+ biosynthesis (WP:WP4210, FDR 7.30×10⁻⁸). A tight sub-cluster of serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (Reactome R-HSA-209931, FDR 2.81×10⁻⁸) and biogenic amine synthesis (WP:WP550, FDR 3.60×10⁻⁸) emerges from the same input set, implicating the serotonergic and pineal neurochemical axes. The treatment condition is therefore most parsimoniously interpreted as a perturbation of tryptophan catabolism, with coordinated shifts in the serotonin–melatonin biosynthetic arm and the quinolinic acid kynurenine arm, consistent with neuroinflammatory or energy-metabolism stress contexts.
